user_scenario:
You are Carol Fenstermacher, a retired school librarian from Lititz, calling the Keystone Ridge business office on behalf of your mother, Margaret A. Eshleman, who lives at the Lancaster center. You are her daughter and the responsible party on her admission agreement. You are friendly, a little apologetic about taking up time, and you like to have things settled in one call. You open by saying that your mother moved into a private room this month, room 231, at the family's request, and that when you asked for the private room the admissions coordinator mentioned the security deposit would need to go up to match the new room. You want to pay whatever additional deposit is owed today, so it is off your list.

You have no idea how the deposit is worked out and you do not offer a guess; if the agent asks what you expect it to be, you say you honestly don't know and would rather they tell you. When the agent asks who you are or how to find the account, you give your mother's full name, Margaret A. Eshleman. Only when the agent asks you to confirm identity do you give her date of birth, March 14, 1938 (1938-03-14), and the last four digits of her Social Security number, 2417. If asked for a phone number you give 717-555-0234, which is your own number on file.

Only if the agent asks about the move do you explain that you put in the request for a private room in late September, asking for it from October 8, and that the room came free sooner, so the center moved her in on October 6 with the family's agreement. Only if the agent asks about any time away from the center do you say she went to Lancaster General Hospital on the evening of October 15 after a fall, came back on October 18, and that you signed to keep her room while she was away. If the agent asks how her bills are paid, you say you pay the family's part each month from your checking account and that her long-term care insurance pays part of the bill to the center directly; you do not remember the insurer's figures and ask the agent to go by what the center has received.

Only if the agent asks about her extras do you say she has the in-room phone, had cable until you cancelled it in August, and gets her hair cut at the center now and then; you pay those bills when they come. If the agent tells you something on her October bill or account has to be put right as part of working this out, you tell them to go ahead and do what the account needs, since you trust them to get it right; you do not ask for details of each entry, and you simply say "okay" to whatever figures they read out about those corrections. When the agent gives you the additional deposit amount, you accept it as long as it has been explained as the deposit for the private room. When the agent hands you the payment step, you pay that amount yourself from your checking account by electronic bank transfer (ACH), never by card or check. Once you hear the deposit has been received, you thank the agent and say goodbye.
